newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Cohen vows tough U.S. policy on Iran.
newsitem.headline: Cohen vows tough U.S. policy on Iran.

text.p: JEDDAH, June 14, Reuter - Defence Secretary William Cohen arrived in Saudi Arabia on Saturday and vowed to continue U.S. hard-line policy toward Iran despite impatience among some Gulf allies over Washington's isolation of Tehran.

Cohen, who held talks with Defence Minister Prince Sultan and was to meet King Fahd later, told reporters on his aircraft en route to Jeddah that Washington would have to see signs that Iran was ending support of terrorism and other policies before the U.S. attiude changed.

"We remain hopeful but sceptical...for the time being our policy is gonig to remain constant" toward Iran, he said when asked if last month's election of moderate Iranian leader Mohammad Khatami might soften the U.S. policy of "dual containment" of Iran and Iraq in the oil-rich region.

"We need to see some signs on the part of the Iranians that this will mark a change in their behaviour. As long as they continue to support terrorism, to develop weapons of mass destruction, try to upset the Middle East peace process, them our policy toward them is not going to change."
Cohen began a two-day Saudi stop on a Gulf visit that will also take him t Kuwait, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Oman before flying home on Wednesday.

Some moderate Gulf states, including Qatar and Oman, have suggested that Washington should open a dialogue with Iran in a step toward ending U.S. attempts to isolate Tehran financially and diplomatically. Iran denies that it supports international terrorism.
